payload.title: File:Eosphorosuchus lacrimosa (holotype postscrania, YPM VP 41198).png
payload.artist_html: M. Margulis-Ohnuma, A. A. Ruebenstahl, D. L. Meyer & B.-A. S. Bhullar
payload.credit_html: "A short-snouted 'sphenosuchian' with unusual feeding anatomy demonstrates that ecological specialization occurred early in crocodylomorph evolution"
payload.description_html: Photographs of the postcranial elements of Eosphorosuchus lacrimosa. Pubes in anterior view (a), long bones of the leg in dorsolateral view (b), ankle (c), pes in anterior view and osteoderm in dorsal view (d). Within (c), left to right, calcaneum in proximal, medial, posterior, distal and lateral views; astragalus in anterior, dorsal, medial and lateral views; third distal tarsal; fourth distal tarsal in lateral, proximal and medial views. MT III and MT IV are represented by proximal ends only. Pathological distal end of metatarsal is likely MT III. Abbreviations: a ca, articulation with calcaneum; a dt4, articulation with distal tarsal 4; ah, anterior astragalar hollow; a mt, articulation with metatarsal V; cc, calcaneal condyle; cp, calcaneal peg; cs, calcaneal socket; ct, calcaneal tuber; ctr, calcaneal tuber ridge; cvf, calcaneal ventral foramen; dcf, distal calcaneal facet; dr, distal roller; d mt, distal end of metatarsal; fe, femur; ff, fibular facet; fh, femur head; fhg, groove on the edge of femoral head surface depression; fi, fibula; for, foramen on proximal surface of distal tarsal 3; gt, greater trochanter; lc, longitudinal cracks; mf, medial foramen; mp, medial process of the calcaneum; MT I, metatarsal I; MT II, metatarsal II; MT III, metatarsal III; MT IV, metatarsal IV; obf, obturator foramen; os, osteoderm; pcf, proximal calcaneal facet; pg, posterior groove of the calcaneum; ph, phalanx; ppr, proximal posterior ridge; td, tibia distal margin; tf, tibial facet; ti, tibia; tfr, tibial facet ridge. Scale bar is 1 cm.
